about.title: About Budget Calculator - Personal Finance Management
about.description: The Budget Calculator is a personal finance planning tool designed to help you create, track, and review your monthly budget. This calculator allows you to input all sources of income and categorize your expenses to get a clear picture of your spending patterns. Effective budgeting can support financial planning by helping you understand where your money goes each month, identify areas for adjustment, and set realistic savings goals.

faq.a: The 50/30/20 rule suggests allocating 50% of after-tax income to needs (housing, utilities, groceries), 30% to wants (entertainment, dining out), and 20% to savings and debt repayment. This provides a simple framework for balanced budgeting.

faq.q: How much should I save for an emergency fund?
faq.a: A common emergency fund target is 3-6 months of living expenses. Some people start with $1,000 as an initial goal, then gradually build up to cover several months of essential expenses like housing, food, and utilities.

faq.q: How often should I review my budget?
faq.a: Review your budget monthly to track spending patterns and make necessary adjustments. Additionally, conduct a more thorough review quarterly or when your income or major expenses change significantly.

faq.q: What if my expenses exceed my income?
faq.a: If expenses exceed income, prioritize essential expenses first, then look for areas to cut spending. Consider reducing discretionary expenses, finding additional income sources, or negotiating lower rates for services like insurance or utilities.
